content.title: Davis Lane Park Sewer Line Replacement
content.summary: Construction of the sewer line replacement at Davis Lane Park has been completed, with final restoration expected in spring 2025. The park will undergo further improvements, including the design and replacement of pickleball and/or tennis courts, starting after the two-year warranty period for the sewer line ends in summer 2027. Community engagement has been prioritized, and the park's amenities have been restored for public use during the planning phase.
content.body:
## Updates

Updated 1/21/25

Construction is complete. Final restoration at the park will be completed in the spring as weather allows. Thank you for your patience throughout construction.

### Park Improvements Timeline

Updated 6/6/25 - Timelines are estimated and subject to change due to planning, permitting, material acquisition, or other unforeseen delays.

- **Summer 2025 to Summer 2027:**Warranty period for the new sewer line; no new park amenities can be constructed during this time
- **Fall 2025 to Summer 2026:**Amenity replacement feasibility and concept design
- **Fall 2026:**Community engagement and analysis of concepts
- **Fall 2026 to Spring 2027:**Design review process for approved new amenities; construction contract solicitation
- **Summer 2027:**Begin construction on new park amenities

### Park Improvements Update 12/12/24

Following direction from City Council and feedback we received from the community, the City is moving forward with the design and replacement of a pickleball and/or tennis court(s) in the park. As part of this process, preserving the park’s mature trees will be a priority to maintain the natural beauty and shade they provide.

As a reminder, any park improvement project will not begin construction until after the two-year warranty period for the sewer line ends, no sooner than 2027. However, project planning and design will be happening during the two-year warranty period.

In the meantime, the trail at Davis Lane Park has reopened, and site amenities, including the picnic table and bike repair station, have been reinstalled for community use.

Community input was received through public meetings and via the City's online engagement platform, Speak Up Arvada. Feedback results and additional information about engagement efforts are available on the [Davis Lane Park Improvements SpeakUp page](https://publicinput.com/n1477).

To stay up to date on future park improvements, provide your email address below. Thank you for your continued support as we work to enhance Davis Lane Park for the future!

                                             

## Overview

The sewer line that runs underneath Davis Lane Park is reaching both the end of its useful life and capacity limits and needs to be replaced. This project will begin at the southeast corner of Davis Lane Park, move through the park, across Simms Street and up to W 71st Avenue. This project is expected to take 8 to 9 months.

### Project Area Map

![project map of sewer line construction from Davis Lane Park north on Simms to 71st Avenue](/ImageRepository/Document?documentId=3089)

This project has been prioritized as a part of long range planning to address aging and undersized utility infrastructure throughout the city.

The sewer rates Arvada customers pay help repair and replace aging infrastructure. Developers pay fees to support increased capacity needs.  Please visit the [Utilities Transparency page](/661/Utilities-Transparency) for more information about the City’s approach to long range planning and funding utility improvements.

## Timeline

Updated 10/28/24

The project is expected to take **approximately 8 to 9 months.**

**Spring and Summer 2024:**construction in Davis Lane Park

- Tennis courts removed
  - [Use this interactive map](https://arvada.maps.arcgis.com/apps/instant/sidebar/index.html?appid=c622097eba7b4e21813564bad5a53878) to see where other City-maintained tennis, pickleball and combined tennis and pickleball courts are located
- Tree removal as needed, tree replacement will be done in consultation with the City's Arborist
- Trail closures and detours

**Summer and Fall 2024:**construction continues up Simms street toward W 71st Avenue

- **Early November:**trail expected to fully re-open
  - Once the trail is re-opened, some temporary detours may be necessary, but they will be minimal
  - Fully re-opening the park will depend on the ability to place sod (weather dependent in Fall 2024 or delayed to Spring 2025)
- Simms Street single lane closures may be necessary
- 71st Avenue temporary road closures with local access only
- Minor work will be performed at 68th and Pierson

**Winter 2024:**construction finishes on W 71st Ave., project is complete

**2025 and beyond:**park improvements

## What to Expect

Additional construction traffic and noise may be present. Please use caution near the work zone. Use the tabs below to see specific information for each work area.

1. [Davis Lane Park & Ralston Creek Trail](#tabe38af95c-e96a-4880-97da-814231be3bdd_0)

Construction is expected to begin as soon as June 3 and take approximately 2 to 3 months.

- Working hours 7 am to 7 pm
- Construction fencing will be in place
- Tennis court removal
- Playground closure as needed to ensure safety near work zone
  - Approx. 1 month
  - Playground will re-open once construction moves a safe distance from the playground area
- Ralston Creek Trail closure through the park (estimated through October 2024)
  - See detour map below
  - Additional detour signage will be in place
- Tree removal and revegetation
  - Tree replacement will take place in consultation with the City Arborist after the project is complete
- Trail underpass at Simms is expected to remain open during most of construction
  - Please note: the underpass may be closed due to safety concerns and proximity to construction

1. [Simms Street](#tabe38af95c-e96a-4880-97da-814231be3bdd_1)

- Beginning in August for approximately 2 months
- Single lane closures may shift between north and southbound lanes
  - Flaggers and signage will be used as needed
- Working hours are 8:30 am to 3:30 pm
  - Hours may be extended 7 am to 7 pm to complete work as quickly as possible

1. [W 71st Avenue](#tabe38af95c-e96a-4880-97da-814231be3bdd_2)

- Local sewer shut offs may be necessary
  - Impacted residents will be notified
- Alternating one-way traffic with local resident access only
  - Flaggers and signage will be used to direct traffic as needed
- Repaving W 71st Ave for areas disturbed upon construction completion

1. [Contact](#tabe38af95c-e96a-4880-97da-814231be3bdd_3)

Please submit questions through [Ask Arvada](/898). This is the most efficient way for the appropriate City team member to respond.
